mutations.because: A page is 100 threads. Stopping after the first one judges a PR on its first hundred and calls the rest clean — an open finding on page two is invisible, which is the shape of the gap X13 records: the merge condition holding on a PR it was never fully asked about. The gate reads two pages precisely so this mutation has somewhere to hide.
command: one unresolved thread on the second page is refused and named

mutations.because: An unreadable page must be 'could not decide', never 'no threads': a partial read that merges is a guess dressed as a verdict, and it fails silently — the one outcome a gate must not have. This is the mutation that turns the tool from a check into a rubber stamp, and it is why the refusal says 'could not decide' rather than reporting a count.
command: a GraphQL error on the second page refuses as could-not-decide

mutations.because: The other way to lose the threads: read every page and then ignore what they said. A gate that never sees an open thread merges straight through a review that is still waiting for an answer, which is the exact regression the wave's merge discipline exists to prevent.
command: one unresolved thread on the second page is refused and named

mutations.because: The head re-check is the half of the condition the script already half-had: it verified checks on a SHA and merged by PR number. Drop the comparison and a push landing after the check read rides in on another commit's green — the race that held #381 together by luck alone. The operator is told both SHAs so the failure names what moved.
command: a head that moved is refused, naming both SHAs
